text:
maria: Quick summary from the replay vs synth runs this morning — apples-to-apples note first: synthetic runner had been using a tight client read loop; replay harness preserved original client read timings. That alone flips p95 for streaming when chunk-size > 1k.

aj: Important. Can you share the exact flags you used so we can reproduce? Also how did you handle KV cache warm/cold? :thinking:

maria: Sure — harness command (run on bench-03):

```
./replay-bench --replay-file=../replays/2026-03-chat-session-8k.json \
  --preserve-iat=true \
  --client-read-mode=chunked \
  --chunk-bytes=512 \
  --concurrency=40 \
  --kv-warmup=1000
```

We ran synth with the same concurrency and a `--client-read-mode=fastloop` for the control. KV warmup = number of requests to preload KV per model variant (so "warm" means ~>99% cache hits).

sam: Profiling notes: when streaming p95 regressed the flamegraphs point to two things: memcpy on the client path (reading chunks) and kernel selection overhead when sequence length jumps. perf snippet:

```
# perf top sample
  12.4%  libinference.so  [.] __memcpy_avx2
  7.1%   libkernelselector.so  [.] choose_kernel_for_seq
  5.6%   libcuda.so  [.] cuLaunchKernel
```

If client read loop yields many small reads we see more copies and context switches. Synth fastloop hides that.

liam: FYI I noticed a perf regression after the kernel selector change in commit `c0f9b2e` — it added a fallback path for quantized kernels that checks multiple kernel candidates at runtime. On long sequences (>2k) that runtime check is non-trivial and shows up in p99 when streaming. Reverting that check reduces p99 by ~12% in our limited runs.

anita: Proposed mitigations:
- For bench parity, make both harnesses expose `--client-read-mode` with explicit semantics: `chunked`, `windowed`, `fastloop`.
- Add a KV warmup phase that documents hit rate target (e.g., target 95% hit).
- When comparing kernels, lock kernel selection to a deterministic policy (env var `FORCE_KERNEL=myfav`) so we measure kernel perf in isolation.

Example regen script:
```
./bench.sh --mode=replay --read-mode=chunked --chunk-bytes=512 --kv-warmup=1000 --force-kernel=matmul_fast_fp16
```

maria: +1 to all. Also we should standardize percentile buckets: always report p50/p90/p95/p99 and tail-samples count.

aj: Could we add a tiny shim in the synthetic client that deliberately mimics the OS-level read behavior? e.g., randomize sleep(0..5ms) between reads to approximate real clients. That would close the gap.

sam: I ran an A/B that adds `--client-read-jitter=0.5ms` to synth and p95 moved ~6% towards replay numbers. So yes, client-side behavior is a first-order effect.

liam: For the kernel selection regression investigation I recommend:
1) Add a micro test that exercises sequence length transitions (512->2048->512) while pinning the kernel selector to measure branch cost.
2) Add counters around the selector to measure how often fallback checks run in steady state.

deploy-bot: Bench run finished: https://bench.internal/runs/1771009876 (summary)
- replay/chunked/kv-warm: p50 38ms p95 210ms p99 430ms
- synth/fastloop/kv-warm: p50 22ms p95 160ms p99 310ms
- replay/chunked/kv-cold: p95 980ms (KV cold dominates)

maria: Action items from thread:
- [aj] add `--client-read-mode` docs and make synth expose `--client-read-jitter` (due EOD)
- [sam] add perf counters in kernel selector and capture flamegraphs for the failing runs
- [liam] run the kernel pinned microbench and open PR to gate runtime fallback behind a config flag
- [anita] extend replay harness to record and replay exact client read iat distribution and add KV-warmup stage

Please paste microbench logs into the run link and label commits that you want bisected. If anyone wants to shadow me I’ll do a paired run at 11:30 to iterate on selector knobs. :thumbsup:
